gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much power the station draws for itself while it waits. Jackery lists 18 W standby for the Explorer 1000 v2, and The Gadgeteer gives about 10 W idle for the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2. A 24 W heat mat draws about as much as that idle load, so the 1,000 Wh class lasts far less time than its Wh rating suggests.
standout_why: I opened ChatGPT's two cited pages: animalstart.com (smart-thermostat outage article) and pets.co.uk (vivarium winter and power-cut blog). I also opened animalstart's backup-controller article. None of them names a power station model, gives an idle or standby draw, or gives a station's switchover time. The animalstart controller article gives only 'zero transfer time' for a generic UPS. The pets.co.uk page tells readers to 'verify automatic transfer behaviour' without a number. ChatGPT's own answers take 85% of the rated Wh and divide by heater watts, with no allowance for the station's own draw. That method gives 34 h for a 25 W mat on 1,000 Wh. I did not open the other uncited results (petco, breedclarity, petnovaworld).
decides: For low-watt reptile heat (heat mats, and emitters cycling on a thermostat), the station's own draw matters as much as its Wh. On a 24 W mat, the Explorer 1000 v2's listed 18 W standby makes it use 42 W in total, so it runs at most about 25 h, not the 38 h that ChatGPT's method gives. The Elite 200 V2 stays the long-outage pick: about 10 W idle per The Gadgeteer and 1.91 kWh delivered in StorageReview's test, so about 56 h on the same mat. The page should give runtimes as Wh ÷ (heater W + idle W), not Wh × 0.85 ÷ heater W. It should also tell owners to turn off BLUETTI's ECO mode. BLUETTI says ECO turns outputs on and off by itself, and that is a risk when a thermostat drops the load to near zero.

findings.label: Standby power consumption (maker-stated)
findings.note: Jackery's FAQ lists 'Standby power consumption: 18W'. It does not say which outputs are on. Arithmetic for a 24 W heat mat: 1,070 Wh ÷ (24 + 18 W) ≈ 25 h at most, before inverter loss. ChatGPT's method (1,070 × 0.85 ÷ 24) gives about 38 h.

findings.label: UPS switchover time
findings.value: ≤20 ms (Jackery: 'not a 0 ms (no interruption) switching UPS')
findings.note: Same FAQ. It also says Energy Saving Mode and auto power-off can be turned off in the app. No default timeout is given.

findings.label: Idle draw with AC and DC outputs on (reviewer-stated)
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Portable Power Station review – The Gadgeteer (Greg Cleveland, 2025-01-06)
findings.note: The text reads 'Low idle consumption, 10w/h with AC and DC left on' (w/h read as W). It is listed in the review with no test method described, so it is not a confirmed measurement.

findings.label: Measured delivered energy
findings.value: 1.91 kWh out of 2,073.6 Wh rated; 2.44 kWh to recharge
findings.source_title: Portable Power Meets Lab-Grade Reliability: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review – StorageReview (Dylan Dougherty, 2025-04-25)
findings.note: The test load is not stated. Arithmetic for a 24 W mat: 1,910 Wh ÷ (24 + 10 W idle) ≈ 56 h. For a 100 W emitter at half duty (50 W average): 1,910 ÷ 60 ≈ 32 h.

findings.label: UPS switchover time
findings.value: 15 ms (maker claim, not timed by the reviewer)
findings.source_title: Portable Power Meets Lab-Grade Reliability: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review – StorageReview
findings.note: StorageReview's spec table lists 'UPS Switch Time 15ms', and its switchover test saw no interruption. The review also says ECO mode can be toggled on the AC or DC outputs to cut idle power. It gives no threshold or timeout.

findings.label: UPS switchover time
findings.note: BLUETTI's page says 'automatically switches over in just 20ms during a power outage'.

findings.label: ECO mode (auto on/off of outputs)
findings.value: BLUETTI: ECO mode 'automatically turns on/off to conserve energy'. No standby wattage is given.
findings.note: The page also says only 'optimized standby power consumption', with no number. Neither the threshold nor whether ECO is on out of the box is on this page. The page advice is to turn ECO off for a thermostat-switched heater.
